subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (latency & cost targets) - draft
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme-corp.com>, Tom Brooks <tbrooks@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (latency & cost targets) - draft

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on your search for a production inference partner for the new Acme Assistant. As discussed, I'm attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the Technical Evaluation milestone. The attachment includes:

- Success criteria (quality, latency, cost) you can use to pass/fail candidate models
- Proposed model shortlist and rationale
- Benchmark plan (test harness, dataset, metrics) and estimated runtime
- Responsibilities and owners (Acme vs Redwood) and target dates
- Dependencies (security review, infra access, sample data)

Quick highlights (pulled from the MAP draft):
- Benchmark success criteria:
  - Latency: p95 inference latency < 150ms for 512-token prompts (regional test env, single-request)
  - Cost target: infer cost <= $0.0006 / token (amortized with batching suggestions)
  - Quality: macro-avg BLEU/ROUGE/and human eval pass rate >= 85% on your 120 prompt eval set
- Model shortlist: Llama-3-34B (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-7B (dense), redwood-2-16k (if you want a longer-context option) — we'll compete on latency/cost tradeoffs and retrain/finetune needs
- Proposed timeline for technical eval milestone: start 02/21, internal infra tests 02/25, full benchmark run 03/03, decision review 03/10. Target close (contract) end of March (03/31).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm owners for infra/key contacts (who will provision test GPUs / provide sample data).
2) We finalize required dataset and success criteria by 02/18 so our bench team can prepare.
3) We schedule the benchmark run window 03/01-03/04.

Attachment: acme-map-draft-v1.pdf (MAP + benchmark template)
Attachment: acme-benchmark-template.xlsx (eval dataset placeholder)

If that looks good I'll update the MAP with any changes and loop in our bench lead to agree on the exact harness and access.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: acme-map-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 210KB)]

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brooks <tbrooks@acme-corp.com>, Devon Lee <devon@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (latency & cost targets) - draft

Thanks, Marissa — this is super helpful and aligns with what we talked about. A couple of clarifying Qs before we lock things down: 

1) For the latency target (p95 < 150ms @ 512 tokens) — is that assuming a single GPU instance (no batching) or with the batching/caching optimizations you mentioned? We need to set expectations for our infra team.
2) On cost: can you break down the $0.0006/token target into model runtime vs infra amortized cost assumptions?
3) Security/compliance: our security team will require an inventory of what logs/PII (if any) are retained during the bench runs. Can Redwood provide a short statement on data handling for bench runs?

Owners: I'll loop in Devon (infra) to handle provisioning; Tom will be our product evaluator and will run the human eval. I expect Devon can confirm infra availability by 02/18.

Also — happy to move the benchmark window out a week if you need more prep time.

Best,
Alicia
Director of Product | Acme Corp
[Sent from mobile]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Devon Lee <devon@acme-corp.com>, Tom Brooks <tbrooks@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (latency & cost targets) - draft

Great notes — thanks Alicia. Short answers below and embedded changes will be reflected in v1.1 of the MAP (I attached an updated draft).

1) Latency assumption: the p95 <150ms is for a single-request path on a dedicated GPU instance with continuous KV cache enabled (no cross-request batching). If you enable small batching (2-4) latency will increase slightly but cost per token improves; we'll provide both single-request and 95th-percentile batched numbers in the bench report.

2) Cost breakdown: the $0.0006/token target is an end-state blended target assuming quantized model (4-bit) + efficient kernel selection + 50% amortization from batching/caching on throughput workloads. Rough split: model execution ~60%, infra overhead (network, memory, management) ~25%, licensing/other ~15%. We will provide a line-itemed cost model in the final benchmark appendix.

3) Security: Redwood bench runs do not persist customer prompt contents outside the short-lived bench instance. We can run with no-log mode for the eval (no retention), or redact and hash incoming prompts. I'll attach our bench data handling statement to the MAP v1.1.

Updated responsibilities (high level):
- Acme: provide sample eval dataset (CSV, 120 prompts), designate product owner for human eval (Tom), and infra contact to enable GPU test env (Devon). Target: provide by 02/18.
- Redwood: prepare bench harness, provide benchmark template & run, produce bench report + cost model. Target: bench run 03/01-03/04, report 03/08.

Dependencies: security sign-off (expected 02/20), access to sample data (02/18), and infra provisioning (02/18-02/21).

Next step: I'll update the MAP and send v1.1 by EOD today; Vivek will join the kickoff call we discussed (propose 02/21 10am PT). Does that time work for you all?

Attachment: acme-map-draft-v1.1.pdf (MAP update with security statement)
Attachment: acme-benchmark-template.xlsx (updated)

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: acme-map-draft-v1.1.pdf (PDF, 230KB)]

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Tom Brooks <tbrooks@acme-corp.com>, Devon Lee <devon@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (latency & cost targets) - draft

Thanks Marissa — that all makes sense. 02/18 for owners and sample data is fine; Devon confirmed infra availability and he'll provision a test GPU cluster this week. 02/21 10am PT works for the kickoff.

We'll aim to have the 120-prompt eval set to you on 02/18. Tom and I will review the MAP v1.1 and call out any small edits; otherwise we'll proceed with the proposed bench window.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Alicia
Director of Product | Acme Corp
